title: No Phantom Cargo
description: A bulk action against a shipment id that doesn't exist should leave exactly zero trace in the shipments table — not a ghost row, not a partial write, nothing.
successCondition: Record the current total shipment count via `npm run db:psql` (select count(*) from shipments). Call POST /api/admin/shipments/bulk with a single fabricated UUID that doesn't correspond to any real shipment, action "cancel". The response's results shows success: false, error: "Shipment not found", succeeded: 0, failed: 1. Re-querying the shipment count confirms it is EXACTLY unchanged from before the call — the failed lookup never inserted, updated, or otherwise touched the shipments table.
hints: bulkShipmentAction (apps/api/src/modules/admin/service.ts) does a findUnique first and immediately continues to the next item on a miss — no prisma.shipment.update or .create is ever reached for an unknown id.

Use a syntactically valid but non-existent UUID (e.g. change a few characters of a real one) so the request passes basic validation and actually reaches the not-found branch, rather than being rejected earlier for malformed input.
